name: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
description: All 113 articles of the Regulation, each with its official heading, chapter and a one-line summary. The article text is not reproduced.
source_note: Official Journal L, 12 July 2024, as published by the Publications Office of the European Union.

controls.title: Subject matter
controls.description: Sets the purpose: a uniform legal framework for human-centric, trustworthy AI that protects health, safety and fundamental rights while supporting innovation in the internal market.

controls.title: Scope
controls.description: Sets who is covered: providers, deployers, importers, distributors and manufacturers placing AI on the Union market or whose output is used in the Union, and lists the exclusions such as military use and pure research.

controls.title: Definitions
controls.description: Defines the terms used, including AI system, provider, deployer, high-risk, general-purpose AI model, systemic risk, substantial modification and serious incident.

controls.title: AI literacy
controls.description: Providers and deployers take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among their staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

controls.title: Prohibited AI practices
controls.description: Prohibits specified AI practices, including harmful manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, certain predictive policing, untargeted facial image scraping, emotion inference at work and school, and most real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces.

controls.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
controls.description: Sets the rules for classifying an AI system as high-risk: safety components of regulated products and the use cases in Annex III, with an exemption where the system poses no significant risk.

controls.title: Amendments to Annex III
controls.description: Empowers the Commission to amend Annex III by adding or modifying high-risk use cases, under stated conditions.

controls.title: Compliance with the requirements
controls.description: High-risk AI systems must comply with the requirements of this Section, taking into account their intended purpose and the state of the art.

controls.title: Risk management system
controls.description: Providers establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system across the lifecycle of the high-risk AI system, including identifying, evaluating and mitigating risks and testing.

controls.title: Data and data governance
controls.description: Training, validation and testing data for high-risk AI systems meet quality criteria and are subject to data governance practices, including bias examination and, in limited cases, processing of special categories of data.

controls.title: Technical documentation
controls.description: Technical documentation is drawn up before market placement, kept up to date and contains at least the elements in Annex IV.

controls.title: Record-keeping
controls.description: High-risk AI systems technically allow automatic recording of events (logs) over their lifetime to support traceability, post-market monitoring and risk identification.

controls.title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
controls.description: High-risk AI systems are designed to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use their output, and come with instructions for use containing the specified information.

controls.title: Human oversight
controls.description: High-risk AI systems are designed so that natural persons can effectively oversee them during use, to prevent or minimise risks, with measures built in or identified for the deployer.

controls.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
controls.description: High-risk AI systems achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle and declare accuracy metrics in the instructions for use.

controls.title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
controls.description: Sets the obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems, including compliance with the requirements, quality management, documentation, logs, conformity assessment, CE marking, registration and corrective action.

controls.title: Quality management system
controls.description: Providers put a documented quality management system in place covering compliance strategy, design and development controls, testing, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring and incident reporting.

controls.title: Documentation keeping
controls.description: Providers keep the technical documentation, quality system documentation and declaration of conformity at the disposal of authorities for ten years after the system is placed on the market.

controls.title: Automatically generated logs
controls.description: Providers keep the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems, to the extent under their control, for at least six months.

controls.title: Corrective actions and duty of information
controls.description: Providers that find a high-risk AI system is not in conformity take corrective action, withdraw, disable or recall it, and inform distributors, deployers and authorities.

controls.title: Cooperation with competent authorities
controls.description: Providers give competent authorities, on reasoned request, the information and documentation needed to show conformity, and access to logs.

controls.title: Authorised representatives of providers of high-risk AI systems
controls.description: Providers established outside the Union appoint by written mandate an authorised representative in the Union before making their high-risk AI systems available.

controls.title: Obligations of importers
controls.description: Importers verify conformity, documentation, marking and the authorised representative before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, and cooperate with authorities.

controls.title: Obligations of distributors
controls.description: Distributors verify CE marking, documentation and instructions before making a high-risk AI system available, and take corrective action if they find non-conformity.

controls.title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
controls.description: A distributor, importer, deployer or other third party is treated as the provider if they put their name on a high-risk system, modify its purpose or substantially modify it, with duties on cooperation along the AI value chain.

controls.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
controls.description: Deployers of high-risk AI systems use them according to the instructions, assign competent human oversight, ensure input data is relevant, monitor operation, keep logs and inform affected people and workers.

controls.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems
controls.description: Certain deployers, such as public bodies and providers of public services, assess the impact on fundamental rights before first use of a high-risk AI system.

controls.title: Notifying authorities
controls.description: Each Member State designates or establishes a notifying authority responsible for assessing, designating and monitoring conformity assessment bodies.

controls.title: Application of a conformity assessment body for notification
controls.description: Conformity assessment bodies apply to the notifying authority of their Member State for notification, with the documentation required.

controls.title: Notification procedure
controls.description: Notifying authorities notify only conformity assessment bodies that meet the requirements, using the Commission's electronic notification tool.

controls.title: Requirements relating to notified bodies
controls.description: Notified bodies must satisfy organisational, quality management, resource and cybersecurity requirements, remain independent and impartial, and carry adequate liability insurance.

controls.title: Presumption of conformity with requirements relating to notified bodies
controls.description: A conformity assessment body that meets the relevant harmonised standards is presumed to meet the requirements for notified bodies.

controls.title: Subsidiaries of notified bodies and subcontracting
controls.description: Sets the conditions under which a notified body may subcontract tasks or use a subsidiary, and remains responsible for their work.

controls.title: Operational obligations of notified bodies
controls.description: Notified bodies verify conformity of high-risk AI systems under Article 43, inform the notifying authority of their activities and keep documentation available.

controls.title: Identification numbers and lists of notified bodies
controls.description: The Commission assigns a single identification number to each notified body and publishes the list of notified bodies.

controls.title: Changes to notifications
controls.description: The notifying authority notifies the Commission and other Member States of relevant changes to a notification, including restriction, suspension or withdrawal.

controls.title: Challenge to the competence of notified bodies
controls.description: The Commission investigates cases where the competence of a notified body or its continued compliance is in doubt.

controls.title: Coordination of notified bodies
controls.description: The Commission ensures appropriate coordination and cooperation between notified bodies through a sectoral group.

controls.title: Conformity assessment bodies of third countries
controls.description: Conformity assessment bodies from third countries with which the Union has an agreement may be authorised to carry out the activities of notified bodies.

controls.title: Harmonised standards and standardisation deliverables
controls.description: High-risk AI systems and general-purpose AI models that conform to published harmonised standards are presumed to conform to the corresponding requirements.

controls.title: Common specifications
controls.description: The Commission may adopt common specifications where harmonised standards do not exist or are insufficient, and systems conforming to them are presumed compliant.

controls.title: Presumption of conformity with certain requirements
controls.description: High-risk AI systems trained and tested on data reflecting their setting, or certified under a cybersecurity scheme, are presumed to meet the matching requirements.

controls.title: Conformity assessment
controls.description: Sets the conformity assessment procedures: internal control or assessment with a notified body, depending on the system, and reassessment after substantial modification.

controls.title: Certificates
controls.description: Certificates issued by notified bodies follow a prescribed form, language and validity of up to five or four years, and can be suspended or withdrawn.

controls.title: Information obligations of notified bodies
controls.description: Notified bodies inform the notifying authority and other bodies of certificates issued, refused, suspended or withdrawn and of conditions affecting their notification.

controls.title: Derogation from conformity assessment procedure
controls.description: Market surveillance authorities may, on a justified request, authorise a specific high-risk AI system for exceptional reasons of public security or protection of life and health, and the Commission may do so on a Union-wide basis.

controls.title: EU declaration of conformity
controls.description: Providers draw up an EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk AI system and keep it available for ten years.

controls.title: CE marking
controls.description: High-risk AI systems carry a visible, legible and indelible CE marking, or a digital one where provided digitally, followed by the notified body's number where one is involved.

controls.title: Registration
controls.description: Providers and certain deployers register themselves and their high-risk AI systems in the EU database before placing them on the market or putting them into service.

controls.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
controls.description: Sets transparency duties: users are told when they interact with an AI system, synthetic content is marked in a machine-readable way, and deployers disclose emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, deep fakes and AI-generated public-interest text.
controls.category: Chapter IV: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

controls.title: Classification of general-purpose AI models as general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
controls.description: A general-purpose AI model is classified as one with systemic risk if it has high-impact capabilities, presumed at a training compute threshold of 10^25 floating point operations, or by Commission decision.

controls.title: Procedure
controls.description: Sets the procedure for notifying the Commission that a general-purpose model meets the systemic-risk threshold and for designation, contestation and reassessment.

controls.title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
controls.description: Providers of general-purpose AI models keep technical documentation, give information to downstream providers, set a copyright compliance policy and publish a summary of training content.

controls.title: Authorised representatives of providers of general-purpose AI models
controls.description: Providers of general-purpose AI models established outside the Union appoint an authorised representative in the Union before placing the model on the market.

controls.title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
controls.description: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk perform model evaluation including adversarial testing, assess and mitigate systemic risks, report serious incidents and ensure adequate cybersecurity.

controls.title: Codes of practice
controls.description: The AI Office encourages and facilitates codes of practice at Union level to help providers of general-purpose AI models apply the Regulation.

controls.title: AI regulatory sandboxes
controls.description: Each Member State ensures that at least one AI regulatory sandbox is operational at national level by 2 August 2026.
controls.category: Chapter VI: Measures in support of innovation

controls.title: Detailed arrangements for, and functioning of, AI regulatory sandboxes
controls.description: The Commission adopts implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements for the establishment, operation, supervision and exit from AI regulatory sandboxes.
controls.category: Chapter VI: Measures in support of innovation

controls.title: Further processing of personal data for developing certain AI systems in the public interest in the AI regulatory sandbox
controls.description: Personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be processed in an AI regulatory sandbox solely for developing certain AI systems in the public interest, under listed conditions.
controls.category: Chapter VI: Measures in support of innovation

controls.title: Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
controls.description: Testing of high-risk AI systems in real-world conditions outside sandboxes is allowed under a plan approved by the market surveillance authority and with safeguards for participants.
controls.category: Chapter VI: Measures in support of innovation

controls.title: Informed consent to participate in testing in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
controls.description: Participants in real-world testing outside sandboxes give freely given, informed consent beforehand, documented and with the right to withdraw.
controls.category: Chapter VI: Measures in support of innovation

controls.title: Measures for providers and deployers, in particular SMEs, including start-ups
controls.description: Member States take measures for SMEs and start-ups, including priority access to sandboxes, awareness and training, and communication channels.
controls.category: Chapter VI: Measures in support of innovation

controls.title: Derogations for specific operators
controls.description: Microenterprises may comply in a simplified way with certain elements of the quality management system required by Article 17.
controls.category: Chapter VI: Measures in support of innovation

controls.title: AI Office
controls.description: The Commission develops Union expertise and capability in AI through the AI Office, supported by Member States.

controls.title: Establishment and structure of the European Artificial Intelligence Board
controls.description: Establishes the European Artificial Intelligence Board, with one representative per Member State, to coordinate and advise on application of the Regulation.

controls.title: Tasks of the Board
controls.description: Lists the tasks of the Board, including advising on implementation, supporting national authorities and contributing to guidelines and codes.

controls.title: Advisory forum
controls.description: Establishes an advisory forum of stakeholders to provide technical expertise to the Board and the Commission.

controls.title: Scientific panel of independent experts
controls.description: The Commission establishes a scientific panel of independent experts to support enforcement, in particular for general-purpose AI models.

controls.title: Access to the pool of experts by the Member States
controls.description: Member States may call upon experts of the scientific panel to support their enforcement activities, subject to fees.

controls.title: Designation of national competent authorities and single points of contact
controls.description: Each Member State designates at least one notifying authority and one market surveillance authority as national competent authorities and notifies a single point of contact to the Commission.

controls.title: EU database for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
controls.description: The Commission sets up and maintains an EU database of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, with specified information that is publicly accessible.
controls.category: Chapter VIII: EU database for high-risk AI systems

controls.title: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan for high-risk AI systems
controls.description: Providers establish a documented post-market monitoring system proportionate to the AI technology and risks, based on a post-market monitoring plan.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Reporting of serious incidents
controls.description: Providers of high-risk AI systems report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities within set time limits, between 2 and 15 days depending on severity, and investigate them.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Market surveillance and control of AI systems in the Union market
controls.description: Applies Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance to AI systems, and sets the powers and organisation of market surveillance authorities.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Mutual assistance, market surveillance and control of general-purpose AI systems
controls.description: The AI Office monitors and supervises AI systems built on a general-purpose model by the same provider, and authorities cooperate on mutual assistance.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Supervision of testing in real world conditions by market surveillance authorities
controls.description: Market surveillance authorities supervise testing in real-world conditions and may require changes, suspension or ending of the test.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Powers of authorities protecting fundamental rights
controls.description: National authorities that protect fundamental rights may request and access documentation created under this Regulation, and cooperate with market surveillance authorities.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Confidentiality
controls.description: Authorities and bodies that apply the Regulation respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained, including trade secrets and source code.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Procedure at national level for dealing with AI systems presenting a risk
controls.description: Sets the national procedure for dealing with AI systems that present a risk: evaluation, required corrective action, withdrawal or recall, and notification to the Commission and other Member States.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Procedure for dealing with AI systems classified by the provider as non-high-risk in application of Annex III
controls.description: Sets the procedure for dealing with AI systems that the provider classified as not high-risk but which a market surveillance authority considers high-risk.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Union safeguard procedure
controls.description: Sets the Union safeguard procedure for assessing national measures against AI systems when other Member States or the Commission object.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Compliant AI systems which present a risk
controls.description: Where a compliant AI system nevertheless presents a risk to health, safety or fundamental rights, the authority requires appropriate measures within a set period.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Formal non-compliance
controls.description: Sets the rules for formal non-compliance such as missing CE marking, declaration of conformity or registration, with required correction and, if not remedied, restriction or withdrawal.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Union AI testing support structures
controls.description: The Commission designates Union AI testing support structures to provide independent technical or scientific advice to authorities.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Right to lodge a complaint with a market surveillance authority
controls.description: Any person with grounds to consider the Regulation has been infringed may lodge a complaint with a market surveillance authority.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
controls.description: Persons subject to a decision of a deployer based on a high-risk AI system with legal or similarly significant effects have the right to clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the system and the main elements of the decision.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Reporting of infringements and protection of reporting persons
controls.description: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 on the protection of persons who report breaches of Union law applies to reports of infringements of this Regulation.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Enforcement of the obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models
controls.description: The Commission has exclusive powers to supervise and enforce the obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models and entrusts the tasks to the AI Office.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Monitoring actions
controls.description: The AI Office may take the actions necessary to monitor effective implementation and compliance by providers of general-purpose AI models, and downstream providers may lodge complaints.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Alerts of systemic risks by the scientific panel
controls.description: The scientific panel may give a qualified alert to the AI Office where it suspects a general-purpose model poses a concrete systemic risk or meets the classification criteria.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Power to request documentation and information
controls.description: The Commission may request documentation and information from the provider of a general-purpose AI model, including by decision.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Power to conduct evaluations
controls.description: The AI Office may conduct evaluations of a general-purpose AI model to assess compliance or to investigate systemic risks, including through independent experts.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Power to request measures
controls.description: The Commission may request providers of general-purpose AI models to take measures to comply, mitigate systemic risk, or restrict, withdraw or recall the model.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Procedural rights of economic operators of the general-purpose AI model
controls.description: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on procedural rights of economic operators applies to providers of general-purpose AI models.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

controls.title: Codes of conduct for voluntary application of specific requirements
controls.description: The AI Office and Member States encourage voluntary codes of conduct that apply some of the high-risk requirements to other AI systems, including on environmental sustainability, AI literacy and inclusive design.
controls.category: Chapter X: Codes of conduct and guidelines

controls.title: Guidelines from the Commission on the implementation of this Regulation
controls.description: The Commission develops guidelines on practical implementation, including the high-risk requirements, prohibited practices, incident reporting and the definition of an AI system.
controls.category: Chapter X: Codes of conduct and guidelines

controls.title: Exercise of the delegation
controls.description: Governs how the Commission exercises its power to adopt delegated acts: five-year period, revocation and the objection period.
controls.category: Chapter XI: Delegation of power and committee procedure

controls.title: Committee procedure
controls.description: Establishes the committee procedure by which the Commission is assisted when adopting implementing acts.
controls.category: Chapter XI: Delegation of power and committee procedure

controls.title: Penalties
controls.description: Member States lay down effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties, with administrative fines of up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover for prohibited practices and lower ceilings for other breaches.

controls.title: Administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
controls.description: The European Data Protection Supervisor may impose administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.

controls.title: Fines for providers of general-purpose AI models
controls.description: The Commission may fine providers of general-purpose AI models up to 3% of worldwide annual turnover or EUR 15 million for listed infringements.

controls.title: Amendment to Regulation (EC) No 300/2008
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EC) No 300/2008 on civil aviation security to take the AI Act's high-risk requirements into account.

controls.title: Amendment to Regulation (EU) No 167/2013
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) No 167/2013 on agricultural and forestry vehicles to take the AI Act's high-risk requirements into account.

controls.title: Amendment to Regulation (EU) No 168/2013
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 on two- or three-wheel vehicles to take the AI Act's high-risk requirements into account.

controls.title: Amendment to Directive 2014/90/EU
controls.description: Amends Directive 2014/90/EU on marine equipment to take the AI Act's high-risk requirements into account.

controls.title: Amendment to Directive (EU) 2016/797
controls.description: Amends Directive (EU) 2016/797 on the interoperability of the rail system to take the AI Act's high-risk requirements into account.

controls.title: Amendment to Regulation (EU) 2018/858
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) 2018/858 on motor vehicle type-approval to take the AI Act's high-risk requirements into account.

controls.title: Amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 on civil aviation so that AI safety components are subject to the AI Act's high-risk requirements.

controls.title: Amendment to Regulation (EU) 2019/2144
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 on motor vehicle safety to take the AI Act's high-risk requirements into account.

controls.title: Amendment to Directive (EU) 2020/1828
controls.description: Adds this Regulation to the list of acts in Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828 on representative actions for consumers.

controls.title: AI systems already placed on the market or put into service and general-purpose AI models already placed on the marked
controls.description: Sets transitional rules for AI systems and general-purpose AI models already on the market, including large-scale IT systems and models placed before 2 August 2025.

controls.title: Evaluation and review
controls.description: The Commission assesses yearly whether to amend the lists in Annex III and Article 5, and reports on evaluation and review of the Regulation at set intervals.

controls.title: Entry into force and application
controls.description: Provides that the Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after publication and applies from 2 August 2026, with earlier dates for the general provisions and prohibitions, governance and general-purpose models, and a later date for some regulated products.
